title: Detached DOM nodes and browser memory leaks
hook: A DOM node removed from the document but still referenced in JavaScript is detached — it cannot be painted but still consumes memory until every reference is dropped.

blocks.text: **Detached DOM tree**: element removed via `removeChild` or `innerHTML = ''` but JS variable, closure, or WeakMap-strong-value still references it. Browser keeps layout/DOM structures alive. **Retained event listeners** on detached nodes also keep handlers and captured data alive. Common in SPAs with manual DOM manipulation or jQuery-era patterns.

entries.plainDefinition: Not in document but referenced from JS.
entries.example: const el = div; div.remove(); el still exists

entries.plainDefinition: Whole tree detached but held by one ref.

blocks.text: Long-lived admin dashboards that re-render tables without teardown leak thousands of detached `<tr>` nodes — Chrome memory climbs, tab crashes. React/Vue usually handle this; leaks appear in D3 charts, third-party widgets, and global caches of DOM fragments.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Global arrays of DOM nodes for "performance". Forgetting third-party widget destroy(). Saving innerHTML children before replace.

blocks.text: Measure: performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize trend. Detached nodes often hide in chart libraries — call destroy() APIs. Memory tool "Summary → Detached" filter. Pair with listener cleanup.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Never heard of detached DOM. Says removeChild always frees memory. No heap snapshot workflow.

interviewTakeaways: Detached = not in document but JS-referenced.
Shows in Chrome heap snapshot as Detached.
Fix: clear JS refs + remove listeners.
60s: removeChild without dropping JS ref leaks memory. Common in SPA manual DOM. Snapshot → Detached → retainers. Framework unmount helps.
Follow-up: templateCache holding removed tr elements.
commonPitfalls: Weak: cache every rendered row in global array.
Weak: ignore chart library destroy on navigation.
Strong: detached definition + snapshot + clear retainers.
